title: NBA Jersey Quiz: Hard Mode
headline: Can You Name The NBA Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Jersey?
description: A hard NBA jersey quiz: eight tiny squares cut from current NBA jerseys, no numbers, no wordmarks, no logos. Just a collar, an armhole trim or a side panel. Guess the team, reveal the answer, keep score.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from a current NBA jersey, about one fiftieth of the whole picture. No numbers, no wordmarks, no logo patches. What is left is the stuff fans stop noticing: the trim around an armhole, a pinstripe, a side panel.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.hint: Hard mode. No numbers, no logos.
items.piece: White and green trim around the armhole of the green jersey.
items.fact: Boston's green jersey keeps the trim plain: thin white and green bands around the neck and both armholes.

items.piece: Orange and white trim around the armhole of the blue jersey.
items.fact: Blue, white and orange are the three colors of New York City's flag, and they are the three colors of this jersey.

items.piece: Cream armhole trim over the cream, blue and green stripes on the side of the green jersey.
items.fact: The cream is officially Cream City Cream, named for the cream-colored brick Milwaukee was built with. It arrived with the Bucks' 2015 rebrand.

items.piece: Thin white pinstripes on the blue jersey.
items.fact: Pinstripes were on the Magic's first uniforms in 1989, and all three of the uniforms Orlando introduced for 2025-26 have them.

items.piece: Purple and white trim around the armhole of the gold jersey.
items.fact: Jack Kent Cooke, who bought the Lakers in 1965, reportedly disliked the word purple, so he called the team's purple Forum blue.

items.piece: Green and white trim around the armhole of the blue jersey.
items.fact: Minnesota's colors since 2017 include midnight blue, aurora green and lake blue, each tied to a part of the Minnesota landscape.

items.piece: The red and white diagonal stripe crossing the black jersey.
items.fact: Frank Glickman designed the pinwheel logo in 1970. The two sets of five lines stand for the five players on each team.

items.piece: Gold trim around the armhole of the royal blue jersey.
items.fact: Golden State went back to royal blue and gold in 2010, with the new eastern span of the Bay Bridge in the logo.
